newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 19.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5649. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- China's Deng Xiaoping on Monday was critically ill and transfered to a hospital in Beijing, a Tokyo source said on Tuesday.
- The government is speeding up diplomatic efforts to bring to Seoul Hwang Jang-yop and his assistant who are seeking asylum in the South Korean embassy in Beijing.

- Kim Hyun-chul, second son of President Kim Young-sam, on Tuesday lodged a criminal libel complaint with prosecutors, saying that six opposition lawmakers had defamed him over the Hanbo loan scandal.
- North Korea has requested a postponement of a controversial shipment of nuclear waste to the stalinist state, a Taiwanese English-language newspaper reported on Tuesday.
- The nation's businesses are facing difficulties and the rate of loan defaults are increasing, as exports remain level despite the won's continued fall.
